slides.1.title: 🍷 Germany — A Red Wine Country?
slides.1.content: Many drinkers don't realise that around 35% of Germany's vineyards are planted to red grapes. Spätburgunder (the German name for Pinot Noir) now produces world-class reds in Ahr and Baden that rival Burgundy. Climate change has steadily lifted the quality of German reds, making them one of the hottest topics in the global wine scene.
slides.2.title: 🔴 Germany's Main Red Grape Varieties
slides.2.items.0.text: Spätburgunder (Pinot Noir): Germany's finest red, with Ahr and Baden as the standouts
slides.2.items.1.text: Trollinger: a Württemberg specialty — light, fresh, an everyday wine
slides.2.items.2.text: Lemberger (Blaufränkisch): deep colour, firm tannin, excellent in Württemberg
slides.2.items.3.text: Dornfelder: late-ripening, deep colour, fruit-forward; common in Pfalz and Rheinhessen
slides.2.items.4.text: Frühburgunder (Pinot Noir mutation): early-ripening, beautifully floral; star of the Ahr
slides.2.items.5.text: Portugieser: light, low-tannin, with a long history; common in Pfalz
slides.3.title: 🏆 Ahr — Germany's Red Wine Heartland
slides.3.content: Ahr is Germany's most famous red wine region, made by Spätburgunder. Although it sits in the country's north (50.5°N latitude), the steep river valley and volcanic-slate soils create a warm microclimate that allows Pinot Noir to ripen fully. Top Ahr Spätburgunder shows Burgundian elegance — bright ruby colour, red berries and spice, refined tannins — turning heads worldwide.
slides.4.title: 🍷 Spätburgunder Showdown: Four Major Regions
slides.4.description: An interactive deep-dive comparing Ahr (volcanic slate, light and mineral) × Baden (warmest, full-bodied, Burgundian) × Pfalz (balanced, easy-drinking) × Württemberg (traditional Muschelkalk chalkiness) — covering the style spectrum, soils, top vineyards (Ahr: Meyer-Näkel; Baden: Bernhard Huber) and comparison with Burgundy. One interactive view captures Germany's four red wine giants.
slides.5.title: Quick Quiz
slides.5.questions.0.question: Spätburgunder is the German name for which variety?
slides.5.questions.0.explanation: Spätburgunder literally means 'late-ripening Burgundian variety' in German — i.e. the French Pinot Noir. In Ahr and Baden, Spätburgunder produces Germany's finest red wines.
